scope: Independent gate review of the 1300-1328 France two-sided interval anchor

evidence_findings: Goldstone's 18-20 million is an observed/reconstructed pre-Black-Death population range, not an independently measured carrying-capacity interval.
Davis supports demographic regulation and resource pressure around 1300, but supplies no numerical saturation fraction.
Lot's 20-24 million values depend on disputed hearth-to-person extrapolation and cannot establish an ecological upper endpoint.
The previous 0.85-1.00 saturation interval was a modeling assumption rather than a literature-supported interval.
The France boundary crosswalk is defensible at 96.21% coverage, so mapping is not the reason for the downgrade.
retained_use: Use 18,000,000 as a conservative one-sided local-food lower-bound test.
Retain the historical 18-20 million population reconstruction and 20-24 million extrapolations as held-out validation context, never as a two-sided capacity target.
Do not add a regional multiplier or adjust the physical model specifically for France.

replacement_search.reason: The existing packet has stronger marginal-land, wage and local-pressure evidence and remains the primary European scale anchor.
Population or ecological limits are available, but a dated, independently supported saturation fraction for the mapped boundary is not.
The records provide population observations, but local-food saturation and boundary-specific pressure evidence are not yet independent enough for a two-sided capacity target.

review.final_status: No independent European replacement two-sided anchor was found in this review. The evidence gate is tightened rather than satisfied by an invented upper endpoint.
